_note: HYPOTHETICAL sample foundation content for the fictional company Lumio. Replace with the customer's approved enablement. Headstart does not author foundation content; it adds rep and account context on top.

sections.heading: What Desk is
points: Desk is the core ticketing product. Every Lumio customer runs on it, so Desk conversations are about expanding and protecting the platform, not landing it.
Email, chat and web forms become tickets in one shared inbox with roles and permissions for agents, leads and admins.

sections.heading: What's new
points: 9.2: SCIM provisioning and SSO enforcement (Okta, Azure AD), included in every plan. Leavers lose access automatically.
9.2: Audit log for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 evidence, in the Desk Shield add-on (+15% of the Desk subscription).
9.3: EU data residency in the Frankfurt region, in the EU Data Residency add-on (+20%).
9.4: Salesforce 360 sync, a two-way sync between tickets and Salesforce accounts, included in every plan.

sections.heading: Who cares
points: IT & Security Admin: SSO, provisioning, audit, residency. They can block a renewal, so bring them in early.
Support Operations Manager: Salesforce sync removes copy and paste between tools.
Head of Support: owns the budget for add-ons.

sections.heading: Discovery questions
points: How do you remove a leaver's access to the helpdesk today, and how long does it take?
When auditors ask who changed a ticket or a setting, what do you show them?
Do any of your customer contracts require data to stay in the EU?
How do account managers find out about open support issues before a call?

sections.heading: Handling objections
points: "SSO should be free." It is: SCIM and SSO enforcement are included in every Desk plan since 9.2. Only the audit log is in Desk Shield.
"We'll just export logs ourselves." Desk Shield's audit log is tamper-proof and covers admin and ticket changes, which is what SOC 2 assessors ask for.

questions.prompt: A customer's IT lead wants leavers removed from the helpdesk automatically. What do they need?
options: Nothing extra: SCIM provisioning is included in every Desk plan
questions.explain: SCIM provisioning and SSO enforcement shipped in Desk 9.2 and are included in every plan.

questions.prompt: Which add-on includes the audit log for SOC 2 and ISO 27001?
questions.explain: The audit log is in Desk Shield, priced at +15% of the Desk subscription.

questions.prompt: Where is ticket data hosted with the EU Data Residency add-on?
questions.explain: Desk 9.3 hosts all ticket data in the Frankfurt region.

questions.prompt: What does Salesforce 360 sync (Desk 9.4) add?
options: A one-way export of tickets to Salesforce
Two-way sync between tickets and Salesforce accounts
questions.explain: It is a two-way sync, so account managers see open tickets in the CRM and agents stop copying data.

questions.prompt: What is the EU Data Residency add-on priced at?
questions.explain: EU Data Residency is +20% of the Desk subscription.

questions.prompt: Which persona is most likely to block a Desk renewal over compliance?
questions.explain: IT & Security Admins own access, compliance and data protection.

sections.heading: What Knowledge is
points: A branded help centre and self-service portal that deflects repetitive how-to tickets, plus a private agent knowledge base with guided onboarding paths.
Priced per agent seat. It pays back fastest where a large share of tickets are simple, repeated questions.

sections.heading: What's new
points: 2.4: Auto-translate publishes every article in 32 languages, with human review for key pages. Included.
2.6: Content freshness alerts flag stale and outdated articles. Included.
2.6: Gap finder clusters tickets that have no article and tells the team what to write next. Included.

sections.heading: Who cares
points: Knowledge & Enablement Lead: owns the help centre and agent onboarding; feels stale content and gaps first.
Head of Support: cares about deflection and the cost of new markets.

sections.heading: Discovery questions
points: What share of your tickets could a customer answer themselves with the right article?
How long does it take a new agent to work without help?
How do you know an article is out of date?
Which languages do your customers ask for help in?

sections.heading: Handling objections
points: "We tried a help centre and nobody used it." Gap finder and freshness alerts tackle the usual cause: missing or stale content.
"Translation is too expensive." Auto-translate is included in every Knowledge plan.

questions.prompt: How many languages does Auto-translate (Knowledge 2.4) publish articles in?
questions.explain: Auto-translate publishes every article in 32 languages, with human review for key pages.

questions.prompt: How are Auto-translate, freshness alerts and Gap finder packaged?
options: All three are included in every Knowledge plan
All three need the Knowledge Pro add-on
questions.explain: All three are included, which makes them strong adoption and cross-sell openers.

questions.prompt: A Knowledge Manager says they write content on gut feel. Which capability answers that?
questions.explain: Gap finder clusters tickets with no article and suggests what to write next.

questions.prompt: What do content freshness alerts do?
options: Flag stale and outdated articles when the product or answers change
Send articles to customers by email
questions.explain: They flag stale and outdated articles so the team fixes them before customers see them.

questions.prompt: Which part of Knowledge helps new agents ramp faster?
options: The internal agent knowledge base with guided onboarding paths
questions.explain: The private agent knowledge base includes guided onboarding paths.

questions.prompt: Which account is the strongest fit for the self-service portal?
options: One where most tickets are complex escalations
One where a large share of tickets are repeated how-to questions
One with no help centre budget
One that only supports by phone
questions.explain: Deflection pays back fastest where many tickets are simple, repeated questions.

sections.heading: What Insights is
points: Analytics for support teams: volume and backlog reports, CSAT surveys and sentiment tagging, out of the box.
Insights Pro (+30% of the Insights subscription) adds prediction and planning.

sections.heading: What's new
points: 5.0: SLA Breach Predictor warns team leads up to four hours before a breach. Insights Pro.
5.0: Executive dashboards, scheduled board-ready packs that replace the monthly spreadsheet. Insights Pro.
5.2: Workforce forecasting predicts volume by hour and channel and builds staffing rosters. Insights Pro.

sections.heading: Who cares
points: Head of Support: CSAT, executive reporting, headcount cases to finance.
Support Operations Manager: SLAs, rosters, peaks.

sections.heading: Discovery questions
points: When did you last breach an SLA, and when did you find out?
How long does the monthly leadership report take to build?
How do you decide how many agents to roster for a peak?
When CSAT drops, how do you find out why?

sections.heading: Handling objections
points: "We already have BI." Insights works on live ticket data with support-specific models (SLA risk, volume forecasts) that a BI team would have to build and maintain.
"Pro is expensive." One avoided SLA penalty or one right-sized peak roster usually covers the 30% uplift.

questions.prompt: How far ahead does the SLA Breach Predictor warn team leads?
questions.explain: It warns up to four hours before a breach.

questions.prompt: Which add-on includes the SLA Breach Predictor, Executive dashboards and Workforce forecasting?
questions.explain: All three are in Insights Pro, priced at +30% of the Insights subscription.

questions.prompt: A Support Ops Manager was understaffed in January and overstaffed in August. What do you lead with?
questions.explain: Workforce forecasting predicts volume by hour and channel and builds rosters for every peak.

questions.prompt: What replaces the monthly leadership spreadsheet?
questions.explain: Executive dashboards are scheduled, board-ready packs (Insights Pro).

questions.prompt: Which Insights capability is included without Pro?
questions.explain: Standard reports, CSAT surveys and sentiment tagging are core Insights.

questions.prompt: What is the Insights Pro uplift?
questions.explain: Insights Pro is +30% of the Insights subscription.

sections.heading: What Automate is
points: Routing, workflows and AI assistance on top of Desk. The no-code workflow builder handles approvals, refunds and escalations.
Automate Copilot (+35% of the Automate subscription) adds the generative AI features.

sections.heading: What's new
points: 3.0: Smart Routing reads every new ticket, detects intent, language and urgency, and routes it to the right queue and agent. Included.
3.0: Approval chains, multi-step approvals for refunds and credits, approved from Slack. Included.
3.2: AI Reply Drafts writes an on-brand reply from the knowledge base, cutting handle time. Automate Copilot.
3.2: Virtual Agent 24/7 answers in chat and email overnight and at weekends, handing over to a human when needed. Automate Copilot.

sections.heading: Who cares
points: Support Operations Manager: triage, handle time, approvals. The day-to-day champion.
Head of Support: after-hours coverage and hiring plans. The budget holder for Copilot.

sections.heading: Discovery questions
points: Who decides which team a new ticket goes to, and how long does that take?
What happens to a ticket that arrives at 7pm on a Friday?
How long do agents spend writing a reply versus solving the problem?
How does an agent get a refund approved today?

sections.heading: Handling objections
points: "AI will say the wrong thing." Reply Drafts are drafts: the agent reviews and sends. Virtual Agent hands over to a human when it isn't confident.
"We can't justify Copilot." Start from the hiring plan: if Reply Drafts saves a quarter of handle time, compare that to the next hire.

questions.prompt: What does Smart Routing (Automate 3.0) use to route a ticket?
questions.explain: Smart Routing detects intent, language and urgency and routes to the right queue and agent.

questions.prompt: Which features need the Automate Copilot add-on?
options: AI Reply Drafts and Virtual Agent 24/7
questions.explain: AI Reply Drafts and Virtual Agent 24/7 shipped in 3.2 as part of Automate Copilot (+35%).

questions.prompt: A customer's weekend tickets wait until Monday. What do you lead with?
questions.explain: Virtual Agent 24/7 answers overnight and at weekends and hands over to a human when needed.

questions.prompt: Where can managers approve refunds with Approval chains?
options: Only in the Lumio admin console
questions.explain: Approval chains let managers approve refunds and credits straight from Slack.

questions.prompt: What is the best answer to "AI will say the wrong thing" about Reply Drafts?
options: Agents review and send every draft
Turn it off for complex tickets
questions.explain: Reply Drafts are drafts: the agent stays in control.

questions.prompt: What is the Automate Copilot uplift?
questions.explain: Automate Copilot is +35% of the Automate subscription.

sections.heading: What Voice is
points: Cloud telephony built into Desk. Every call is logged against the ticket, so agents stop switching between a separate phone system and the helpdesk.
Priced per phone agent (about 60% of a typical support team).

sections.heading: What's new
points: 2.0: Call recording with PCI redaction records calls and removes card numbers from recordings. Included.
2.0: Call summaries turn every call into a transcript and AI-written call notes on the ticket. Included.

sections.heading: Who cares
points: Head of Support: one view of every channel; phone capacity.
Support Operations Manager: wrap-up time.
IT & Security Admin: call recording retention and PCI.

sections.heading: Discovery questions
points: Where are phone calls logged today, and can an agent see the last call on a ticket?
How long do agents spend writing notes after a call?
Do customers ever read card numbers out over the phone?

sections.heading: Handling objections
points: "We just renewed our phone system." Start with the team where wrap-up time hurts most and plan the rest for the phone system's renewal date.
"Compliance won't allow recordings." PCI redaction removes card numbers from recordings automatically.

questions.prompt: What does PCI redaction in Voice 2.0 remove from recordings?
questions.explain: It removes card numbers from recordings.

questions.prompt: What do Call summaries add to the ticket?
options: A transcript and AI-written call notes
questions.explain: Every call becomes a transcript and AI-written call notes, so wrap-up time drops to seconds.

questions.prompt: How are Call recording and Call summaries packaged?
options: Both included in every Voice plan
Both in a Voice Pro add-on
Recording included, summaries in Automate Copilot
questions.explain: Both shipped in Voice 2.0 and are included.

questions.prompt: A Head of Support says calls aren't logged against tickets. What is the core Voice message?
options: Voice replaces the separate phone system and logs every call on the ticket
Voice exports call logs to Excel
questions.explain: Cloud telephony inside Desk logs every call against the ticket.

questions.prompt: Roughly what share of a support team is Voice priced for?
questions.explain: Voice is priced per phone agent, about 60% of a typical team.
